text: In the beginning, the old stories say, there was only dark water, and on it, a golden egg.
Hiranya-garbha. The golden womb.
When it broke, one half became the sky, and the other, the earth. And the one who woke inside was Brahma, the creator.
He has four faces, so that he sees in every direction at once. From each of his four mouths came one of the four Vaydas.
asr: He has four faces, so that he sees in every direction at once. From each of his four mouths came one of the four Vedas.

text: In his four hands, he holds what a world needs to begin.
asr: In his forehands, he holds what a world needs to begin.

text: A water pot, for the waters of life.
A string of beads, to count out time.
The sacred Vaydas, for knowledge.
And a lotus, for all that grows pure from the mud.
His mount is the swan, which is said to separate milk from water: the gift of telling the true from the false.
asr: His mount is the swan, which is said to separate milk from water: the gift of telling the true from the falls.

text: Saraswati, goddess of knowledge and music, rides the same white swan.
asr: Sarah Swati, goddess of knowledge and music, rides the same white swan.

text: One day of Brahma lasts four billion, three hundred and twenty million years, and his night is just as long.
asr: One day of Brahma lasts 4 billion, 320 million years, and his night is just as long.

text: He lives for a hundred such years. And then the universe rests.
Few temples are built for him. The best known stands at Pushkar, in Rajasthan, beside a lake said to have formed where his lotus fell.
And the hour before dawn still carries his name: Brahma muhurta, the creator's hour, when the world is about to begin again.
asr: And the hour before dawn still carries his name: Brahma Muherda, the creator's hour, when the world is about to begin again.

text: From his mind, he brought forth sons. Among them were the seven great sages, the Saptarishi.
Their light still turns above us, in the seven stars of the Great Bear.
One flower carries his name. High in the Himalaya, the Brahma kuh-mull opens at night, in the brief summer of the mountains.
asr: One flower carries his name. High in the Himalaya, the Brahma Kamal opens at night, in the brief summer of the mountains.

text: It grows between three thousand and four thousand eight hundred metres, where little else can bloom.
asr: It grows between 3,000 and 4,800 meters, where little else can bloom.

text: Pilgrims come to bathe at its fifty-two ghats, most of all at the full moon of Kartik, in the autumn.
asr: Pilgrims come to bathe at its 52 gats, most of all at the full moon of kartic in the autumn.

text: It begins about an hour and a half before sunrise: a time kept for quiet, for study, and for prayer.
